episode_id: Bring my configuration up to date with the setting names the app uses now. Rename the old key in my own override file, and keep that file out of git./seed-2-config_renamed-25587

reason: negative side failed: preconditions accepted 1 of 2 same-intent states (config_renamed seed 2 resolves to 'migrate_local', which accepts ['migrate_local']), and that is the state the program was compiled from: it declares variant 'rename', but the solution it was compiled from is a 'migrate_local' resolution there, so the declared variant, not the preconditions, is what is wrong

refused_program.body:
set -e
remap=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$remap"' EXIT
git show HEAD:config/renames.conf | awk -F= '
  /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
  NF >= 2 {
    k = $1; v = $2
    gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/, "", k)
    gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/, "", v)
    if (k != "" && v != "") printf "%s\t%s\n", k, v
  }
' > "$remap"
files=()
while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do files+=("$f"); done < <(git ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard -z)
for f in "${files[@]}"; do
  [ -f "$f" ] || continue
  case "$f" in
    *.conf|*.ini|*.cfg|config/*|*/config/*) ;;
    *) continue ;;
  esac
  tmp=$(mktemp)
  awk 'FILENAME == ARGV[1] {
      n = split($0, p, "\t")
      if (n >= 2) {
        k = p[1]; v = p[2]
        gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/, "", k)
        gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/, "", v)
        if (k != "") m[k] = v
      }
      next
    }
    {
      line = $0
      pos = index(line, "=")
      if (pos > 0) {
        key = substr(line, 1, pos - 1)
        t = key
        gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/, "", t)
        if (t in m) {
          lead = key
          sub(/[^ \t].*$/, "", lead)
          tail = key
          sub(/^.*[^ \t]/, "", tail)
          print lead m[t] tail substr(line, pos)
          next
        }
      }
      print
    }' "$remap" "$f" > "$tmp"
  if ! cmp -s "$tmp" "$f"; then
    cat "$tmp" > "$f"
  fi
  rm -f "$tmp"
done
refused_program.intent: Bring the user's own configuration override up to date with the setting names the application uses now: rewrite every stale old key in the git-ignored override file to its current name using the repository's key rename map, and leave that file untracked and ignored so nothing is added to git.

postconditions.description: no ignored config override file still uses an old key name from the rename map
postconditions.name: no_stale_keys_left
postconditions.probe:
stale=0
keys=$(git show HEAD:config/renames.conf | awk -F= '/^[[:space:]]*#/ {next} NF>=2 {k=$1; gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/,"",k); if (k!="") print k}')
while IFS= read -r f; do
  [ -f "$f" ] || continue
  case "$f" in
    *.conf|*.ini|*.cfg|config/*|*/config/*) ;;
    *) continue ;;
  esac
  while IFS= read -r k; do
    [ -n "$k" ] || continue
    pat=$(printf '%s' "$k" | sed 's/[][\\^$.*+?(){}|]/\\&/g')
    if grep -qE "^[[:space:]]*$pat[[:space:]]*=" "$f"; then stale=1; fi
  done <<< "$keys"
done < <(git ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard -z | tr '\0' '\n')
[ "$stale" -eq 0 ]

while IFS= read -r f; do
  [ -f "$f" ] || continue

  esac
  while IFS= read -r k; do

  done <<< "$keys"
done < <(git ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard -z | tr '\0' '\n')
[ "$found" -eq 1 ]
